clue.text: Detrimental, hard, and as much as one can bear

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

blocks.clueFragment: as much as one can bear
blocks.note: the amount you can carry in your arms

explanation.surface: Something damaging is described as tough and almost more than a person can endure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harmful causes damage, which is exactly what detrimental means; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Consort with, ultimately, American gang

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the word before is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of with
US is short for American
a band is a group or gang

explanation.surface: An instruction to associate, in the end, with a US street gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consort with' reads as a verb phrase, but Consort alone is a noun, a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse, especially of a monarch, and a husband is a male spouse.

clue.text: Continued holding Eastern game in Asian city

indicators.note: holding means keeping within, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: ran on means continued
go is a board game from East Asia

explanation.surface: A tournament of an Oriental game carried on in an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangoon is the former name of Yangon, the largest city of Myanmar (Burma).
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon, now Yangon, is the chief city and former capital of Myanmar in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Almost too ironbound? Wrong

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the word loses its last letter
bound means tied round, so iron surrounds the shortened word

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron; the bound part of this word is the wrapping signal
too means also, cut short here

explanation.surface: A query about something nearly too tightly clad in metal, judged incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ironbound' looks like one word but splits into iron and bound.
explanation.definitionFit: False means untrue or incorrect, so it is a synonym of wrong as an adjective.

clue.text: Holder of post I, for example, fight

blocks.note: I is one of the alphabet's letters
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Someone holding an office, perhaps the speaker, ready for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Post means mail; the surface suggests a job or position.
explanation.definitionFit: A letterbox is the slot or box that receives mail, so it holds the post delivered.

clue.text: After reform, time's up? This keeps movement going

indicators.note: a reform reshapes something, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A political shake-up after someone's term ends is what drives a campaign forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the momentum or driving force that keeps a moving body or a process in motion.

clue.text: Showing lack of skill — it holds writer up

indicators.note: holds means keeps inside, so the writer goes within it
up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A clumsy effort, it stalls the author's progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or incompetent, lacking the skill to do a task well.

clue.text: Person taking action that's clear over row

indicators.note: over in a down clue means sitting above, so that word comes first

blocks.note: plain means obvious, clear
a tiff is a quarrel or row

explanation.surface: Someone acting decisively once an argument is obviously done with.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking action here means bringing a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a legal action against another in court.

clue.text: Ornamental piece knitter modified

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: A decorative item that a knitter has adjusted.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket is a small, cheap ornament or piece of jewellery, a decorative bauble.

clue.text: Slim, small type who makes advances

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a lender advances money as loans

explanation.surface: A thin, little person who keeps making passes.
explanation.walkthrough: Advances are loans, not romantic approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender and slim both mean thin in build; they are adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Something worn in solitary confinement, finally

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: solitary means alone, one only
the last letter of confinement

explanation.surface: It sounds like the clothing a prisoner wears while held in isolation.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest, a garment someone wears, so it is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Test explosive device after returning fire

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for fire is read backwards

blocks.note: to fire someone is to axe them
a mine is a buried bomb

explanation.surface: A bomb disposal trial following an exchange of gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the mine second; 'fire' means dismiss from a job, not shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to test or inspect something closely, as in an examination.

clue.text: Portion of what one mentioned as reparation

indicators.note: a portion is a part, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: found across the three words, dropping wh- and -ioned

explanation.surface: A share of what somebody said is offered by way of making amends.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends for a wrong, which is what reparation also means.

clue.text: Like deluded emperor or a king in dreadful end

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a bad state, so the word end is messed up
in places the article and the king inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale ruler, fooled by his tailors, meets a terrible finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The emperor is from Hans Christian Andersen's tale The Emperor's New Clothes, who parades wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The fooled emperor in the fable walks out without any clothes at all, so he is unclothed.

clue.text: Material taken from ground put back

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: ground in the sense of earth that has been dug and mined

explanation.surface: Some substance was dug out of the earth and then returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a cotton twill fabric, a kind of material used for jeans.

clue.text: Fashion rebel introducing new change to be trendy

indicators.note: introducing means bringing inside, so one letter is put within the word for rebel

blocks.note: a mode is a fashion or style
to rise up is to rebel
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fashion rebel brings in something new to stay in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like a verb or an anagram signal; here it is simply the noun mode.
explanation.definitionFit: To modernise is to update something so it suits current tastes, making it up to date.

clue.text: Advocate taking increase, mostly in exchange for something else

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
taking means accepting inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to barter is to trade goods for other goods
a rise is an increase, here without its last letter

explanation.surface: A lawyer accepts a pay rise as part of some trade-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The barter frame holds the shortened rise after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a courtroom lawyer in Britain, one who pleads cases as an advocate.

clue.text: Making good piece of jewellery others love initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the last two words are placed in front

blocks.note: the rest means the others
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a ring is worn as jewellery

explanation.surface: Mending a jewel that others first fell for.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good is to repair or put right, which is what restoring means.

clue.text: Puzzling statements from member of team in processions

indicators.note: in places the team member inside the word for processions

blocks.note: parades are processions
oxen pulling a plough are yoked as a team

explanation.surface: Confusing remarks made by a sportsman marching in parades.
explanation.walkthrough: A team here is a team of oxen, not a sports side.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradoxes are self-contradictory or seemingly absurd statements that puzzle the hearer.

clue.text: Foresee monarch being put into power with decree

indicators.note: being put into means placed inside, so the monarch sits within what follows

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for power
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen
an edict is an official decree

explanation.surface: Anticipating a monarch coming to power through a royal proclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict is to say in advance what will happen, which is to foresee it.

clue.text: Formal attire from Algeria altered

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: Ceremonial dress from North Africa, tailored to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the ceremonial robes and emblems worn on formal occasions, so official dress.

clue.text: Swindle foreign woman and daughter

blocks.note: Frau is German for a woman or wife
D is the abbreviation for daughter; and simply adds it

explanation.surface: A con trick worked by a woman from abroad and her girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud is a deception for gain, a scam or swindle; both work as nouns.

clue.text: In customary way, USA upset, then disrupted, left

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means tipped over, so the letters read from the bottom
disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned over
the same word used a second time, now jumbled
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: America lost again, as it so often does, then left in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: USA does double duty: once turned upside down, then once scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: As usual means in the normal or habitual manner, the customary way of things.

clue.text: Stranger replacing contents of dairy, not stable

indicators.note: replacing the contents means emptying the word and putting something else inside

blocks.note: dairy emptied of its middle leaves only its outside letters
odder means more strange

explanation.surface: An unsteady stranger turns up in place of the dairy goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun for an unknown person; it is the comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Doddery means shaky and unsteady on one's feet, usually from age, so not stable.

clue.text: Like beavers, grow up in European river

indicators.note: in places one word between the letters for European and river

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
to grow up or get older is to age
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A nature note: young beavers mature in a river on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom eager beaver describes a keen, hard-working person.
explanation.definitionFit: From the idiom eager beaver, beavers are proverbially keen and enthusiastic, so the adjective describes them.

clue.text: Hampered by winter weather currently in South, before spring

indicators.note: in places the word for currently within the abbreviation for south

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
currently means at present, now
to spring is to bound or leap

explanation.surface: A weather report: down south, snow is causing trouble until spring arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring is a verb meaning leap here, not the season the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowbound means unable to travel or leave because of heavy snow, the classic winter hazard.

clue.text: Sudden outburst from second mate

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
an ally is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: An angry eruption from the first mate's deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden sortie or a sudden witty or angry remark, an outburst.

clue.text: Meat that can be saved and brought home

definitions.text: that can be saved and brought home

blocks.note: first meaning: cured pork

blocks.clueFragment: that can be saved and brought home
blocks.note: second meaning: what two idioms say you save and bring home

explanation.walkthrough: To save your bacon is to escape trouble; to bring home the bacon is to earn a living. Both idioms use the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pig meat, and the word stars in the idioms about rescue and earning money.

clue.text: Bad feeling I am going to leave to others

blocks.note: I'll is the contraction of I will, I am going to
to will property is to bequeath it

explanation.surface: Someone resents a relative who plans to bequeath everything to other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is hostility or animosity, a bad feeling held toward someone.

clue.text: Embrace uncle I'd mistreated

indicators.note: mistreated means handled badly, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A confession: I hugged the uncle I had treated badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace something can mean to take it in or encompass it, the same as to include it.

clue.text: Essay about old play such as Hamlet

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: to essay is to attempt, try
aged means old

explanation.surface: A school essay on a Shakespeare play from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essay' is the verb meaning attempt, not a written composition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is Shakespeare's best-known tragedy, a serious drama ending in disaster for its hero.

clue.text: Use of firearms spoiled plan fellow conceals

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so the word plan is jumbled
conceals means hides inside, so the fellow wraps the other letters

blocks.note: a guy is a man or fellow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man hides the shooting that wrecked his scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunplay is the firing or brandishing of guns, as in a shoot-out.
